title: Tracking the Stepwise Formation of a Water-Soluble Fluorescent Tb12 Cluster for Efficient Doxorubicin Detection

material_class.structural_family: sandwich-shaped Tb12 cluster of two Tb4 tetrahedra linked by an equilateral triangular Tb4 core

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of H2L (0.30 mmol, 0.0792 g; H2L = N-[5-(5-acetylamino-4H-[1,2,4]triazol-3-ylmethyl)-4H-[1,2,4]triazol-3-yl]-acetamide), Tb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.30 mmol, 0.1370 g), and NaN3 (0.60 mmol, 0.0390 g) was added to 7 mL DMF and 7 mL isopropanol and sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel vessel. The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 20 min, heated at 120 °C for 3 days, then cooled to 25 °C at 5 °C h−1. Colorless block crystals of Tb12 were obtained, washed with filtered stock, and air-dried. Sodium azide was noted as beneficial for crystallization. Caution: sodium azide is highly toxic and explosion-prone.
synthesis.temperature: stirred at room temperature, then 120 °C; cooled to 25 °C at 5 °C h−1
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal synthesis in a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel vessel
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: colorless block crystals washed with filtered stock and dried in air

properties.summary: Water-soluble Tb12 is a yellow-green luminescent cluster used as a fluorescent probe for doxorubicin. Solid-state quantum yield 0.39% and lifetime 1.26 ns; aqueous solution UV absorption at 256 nm and Tb3+ emission at 490, 545, 585, and 622 nm (λex = 265 nm). DOX quenches the emission (up to ~90%) with KSV = 8.7 × 10^5 M−1 and LOD = 13 nM over 33–98 μM, remaining selective in simulated urine/serum interferents. Fluorescence is relatively stable at pH 4.0–12.0.
